summary: This Informational document describes a framework for Computing-Aware Traffic Steering, identifying functional components, their interactions, and example control and data plane workflows. It covers only a single service provider.

eli5.summary: A traffic director sends you to the least busy store, not just the closest.

subtitle: Directing traffic based on network state and computing resource load

tldr.problem: Traditional service routing directs traffic to the closest server by network path without considering actual network congestion or server load, leading to poor latency for latency-sensitive services.
tldr.mechanism: CATS defines functional components (C-SMA for computing metrics, C-NMA for network metrics, C-PS for path selection, C-TC for traffic classification) that collect dynamic state and steer traffic to the service contact instance that best serves each request based on current conditions.
tldr.outcome: Service providers can deploy computing-aware traffic steering in distributed, centralized, or hybrid models, enabling better performance for latency-sensitive applications like AR/VR while maintaining single or multiple service instances.

facts.label: Metric types
facts.value: Computing (CPU, memory, load) and network (latency, congestion)

today: RFC 10053 is an Informational framework document that complements related IETF work on traffic steering and computing. It provides architectural guidance for operators deploying computing-aware traffic steering and references related work like RFC 9522 (traffic engineering) and RFC 10054 (collaborative frameworks). It is used by service providers implementing dynamic routing that accounts for both network and compute resource state.

sections.title: Computing-Aware Traffic Steering Framework
sections.content:
Services once hosted in a single location are now distributed across multiple service sites to address performance and resource constraints. However, traditional network routing directs traffic based on static routing metrics, often selecting the geographically or topologically closest server without considering real-time server load or network congestion.

This document defines a framework called Computing-Aware Traffic Steering (CATS) that enables dynamic, metric-driven steering of traffic toward the service contact instance that best serves each request. The framework identifies functional components, their interactions, and workflows for both control and data planes. By combining computing resource metrics (e.g., CPU load, memory utilization) with network metrics (e.g., latency, congestion), CATS adapts to changes in both infrastructure and service state, benefiting latency-sensitive services like augmented reality, virtual reality, and interactive games.
sections.eli5: Instead of always going to the nearest store, you check which one is least crowded and has the item in stock right now.

sections.title: Functional Components and Identifiers
sections.content:
CATS defines several key functional components. A CATS Service Metric Agent (C-SMA) collects information about the capabilities and status of service sites and service instances, such as available CPU, memory, and the number of active connections. A CATS Network Metric Agent (C-NMA) gathers network state information like link latency, available bandwidth, and congestion conditions.

The CATS Path Selector (C-PS) receives metrics from both agents and uses them to select the Egress CATS-Forwarder (and potentially the specific service contact instance) toward which traffic should be steered, along with the best path to reach it. CATS-Forwarders are network entities that steer traffic along computed paths; Ingress CATS-Forwarders place traffic onto the CATS-computed path, while Egress CATS-Forwarders connect to service sites. A CATS Traffic Classifier (C-TC) associates incoming packets with service requests using identifiers (CS-IDs) and ensures all packets for one service request go to the same contact instance. Services are identified by a CS-ID (Service ID), and specific contact instances by a CSCI-ID (Service Contact Instance ID).
sections.eli5: There is a traffic director who watches both the road and the store, and tells drivers which store to go to.

sections.title: Control and Data Plane Workflows
sections.content:
CATS divides operations into control and data planes. In the control plane, C-SMAs and C-NMAs continuously collect and advertise metrics related to the service (computing metrics) and network (latency, congestion). These metrics are distributed to C-PSes using one of several schemes: distributed protocols (e.g., extensions to routing protocols), centralized collection (e.g., via an SDN controller or Path Computation Element), or a hybrid approach.

In the data plane, when a service request arrives, the C-TC classifies it using the Service ID and coordinates with a C-PS (collocated or remote) to determine the best Egress CATS-Forwarder. The Ingress CATS-Forwarder then encapsulates the traffic and forwards it along the computed path to the selected Egress CATS-Forwarder, which forwards the traffic to the appropriate service contact instance. All packets belonging to the same service request must follow the same path to the same contact instance (service affinity), ensuring consistent service delivery without misordering or unpredictable latency variations.
sections.eli5: The director checks the conditions every moment. When a customer wants a service, the director quickly decides which store and which route to send them to.

sections.title: Distributed, Centralized, and Hybrid Deployment Models
sections.content:
CATS functional components can be deployed in three ways. In a Distributed Model, computing metrics are shared directly among network devices using distributed protocols (like extended routing protocols), and path selection decisions are made by Ingress CATS-Forwarders, which co-locate the C-PS function.

In a Centralized Model, computing and network metrics are collected by centralized control elements (e.g., an SDN controller or PCE), which compute paths and synchronize steering decisions to Ingress CATS-Forwarders. In a Hybrid Model, static capabilities (which change infrequently) are distributed among network devices, while dynamic resource utilization data is collected centrally to avoid flooding the network. Path computation may be performed centrally, at ingress routers, or both, with results shared between the systems. The choice depends on operator preferences, scalability requirements, and network size.
sections.eli5: You could have each store figure out its own best customer (distributed), one headquarters decide for all stores (centralized), or a mix: stores report inventory to headquarters, which routes based on distance and current stock.

sections.title: Operational and Deployment Considerations
sections.content:
Deploying CATS requires provisioning: allocating and binding CS-IDs and CSCI-IDs to service contact instances, providing C-PS elements with optimization metrics and policies, configuring encapsulation capabilities and credentials for CATS-Forwarders, and resetting classification tables. Computing metrics change frequently and may be normalized (converted to unitless scores) or aggregated to reduce state distribution overhead while preserving accuracy.

Supervision and OAM tools are essential to assess correct CATS operations: exposing the classification and encapsulation capabilities of components, retrieving active classification rules and steering decisions, and verifying paths and forwarding behavior. Security considerations include authentication and integrity protection of metric information shared between C-SMAs/C-NMAs and C-PSes to prevent manipulation that could misdirect traffic. This document covers only single service provider scenarios; multi-provider scenarios are out of scope.
sections.eli5: You must teach the network what each service is, what the optimization rules are, and check that everything works correctly.

layers.label: Control Plane
layers.detail: C-SMA, C-NMA, C-PS collect metrics and make steering decisions

layers.label: Data Plane
layers.detail: C-TC and CATS-Forwarders classify packets and forward traffic

items.title: C-SMA
items.text: Gathers computing resource and service instance status (CPU, memory, load)

items.title: C-NMA
items.text: Collects network state (latency, congestion, bandwidth availability)

items.title: C-PS
items.text: Selects best Egress CATS-Forwarder and path based on combined metrics

items.title: C-TC
items.text: Classifies packets by Service ID and ensures flow affinity

items.title: CATS-Forwarders
items.text: Steer traffic along computed paths to selected service contact instance
